title: The retina of Psammodynastes pulverulentus (Boie, 1827) and Telescopus fallax (Fleischmann, 1831) with a discussion of their phylogenetic significance (Colubroidea, Serpentes)
journal: Zeitschrift fur Zoologische Systematik und Evolutionsforschung 28(4): 269-276
why: Simoes et al. 2016 (opened) cite it for the fovea, 'known from very few snakes'; the repfocus Telescopus bibliography (opened) lists the same reference. It is a histology paper on the retina of Telescopus fallax, so it may give the fovea, the photoreceptor types and a cell density for the genus. Authors, year and pages confirmed from two opened pages; no DOI found.

authors: Gower DJ, Sampaio FL, Peichl L, Wagner HJ, Loew ER, McLamb W, Douglas RH, Orlov N, Grace MS, Hart NS, Hunt DM, Partridge JC, Simoes BF
title: Evolution of the eyes of vipers with and without infrared-sensing pit organs (supplementary Tables S2-S4: predicted visual pigment peaks)
journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society 126(4): 796-823
why: The opened accepted manuscript says its predicted pigment peaks for Echis coloratus (and Echis ocellatus, from Simoes 2016) are in Tables S2-S4, after the point where the text cut off. They would give opsin-inferred peaks for the genus Echis, so they bear on the Echis carinatus pigment cell (grade g at most).
get: open access: the City Research Online accepted manuscript, https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/21664/1/Gower_etal_ViperVision_accepted_ms.pdf (the supplementary tables are also on the OUP journal page)
